contentBlocks.title: Local Start-up Assistance through Free Incubation Facilities and Institutional Resources – CAZE Labs Private Limited

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University, through the Kristu Jayanti Incubation Centre (KJIC), supports the establishment and growth of entrepreneurial ventures by providing access to institutional infrastructure, facilities and mentoring resources. As part of this initiative, CAZE Labs Private Limited has been onboarded as an incubatee under a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the institution.
The university extends the following support to CAZE Labs to facilitate its business operations and entrepreneurial development:
Free Office Space: Provides office space at the Kristu Jayanti Incubation Centre without collecting rental charges during the tenure of the MOU.
Broadband Internet Connectivity: Provides wired and wireless broadband internet access to support the company's software development, communication and business operations.
Office Infrastructure: Provides standard essential office furniture and workspace facilities required for day-to-day operations.
Electricity: Extends electricity facilities to support the operational requirements of the start-up.
Registered Office Address: Permits the incubatee to use the Incubation Centre's institutional address for company registration and other related business requirements, subject to the MOU.
Mentoring Support: Facilitates mentoring to strengthen the entrepreneurial and business development capabilities of the incubatee.
Training and Workshops: Provides opportunities to participate in seminars, workshops and training programmes conducted in collaboration with the Incubation Centre.
Research and Student Collaboration: Encourages joint research activities, student internships and projects, promoting interaction between the start-up and the academic community.
Knowledge Sharing: Facilitates knowledge exchange and opportunities for the incubatee to participate in institutional training programmes.

Through these provisions, the university reduces the initial infrastructure and operational expenditure of the start-up by offering essential facilities and institutional resources without rental charges. The initiative demonstrates the university's commitment to providing practical assistance to entrepreneurs through access to infrastructure, mentoring, training and knowledge-sharing opportunities, thereby supporting the development and sustainability of start-up ventures.

Beneficiary: CAZE Labs Private Limited
Supporting Institution: Kristu Jayanti University / Kristu Jayanti Incubation Centre (KJIC)
Nature of Assistance: Free incubation facilities, infrastructure, internet connectivity, utilities, mentoring and entrepreneurial support

contentBlocks.title: Training workshops and access to university resources
1. Interaction with SHG Women: Self-Help Groups and Microfinance (CSA, January 2025)
paragraphs: The Centre for Social Activities of Kristu Jayanti conducted an interactive session for rural women at Shivagange village, Kolar, during its rural exposure camp, with a team of 70 volunteers. The session explained how Self-Help Groups (SHGs) provide financial support, skill development and a platform for collective decision-making. Participants were taught how to form and manage an SHG and why regular saving matters. They were also shown how to access microfinance, which is the usual first source of capital for small rural enterprises. Volunteers shared success stories of other rural SHGs to inspire the women to collaborate, pool resources and improve their economic independence. The session works as a training workshop, in which university students transfer practical knowledge on group enterprise and financial inclusion to the community. A total of 65 women from Shivagange village benefitted. The activity supports financially sustainable livelihoods by building the savings habit and collective entrepreneurship among women, and by connecting them with formal financial channels.

contentBlocks.title: 2. One District One Product (ODOP) and Campus Farmers Market (UBA, 31 January 2025)
paragraphs: On 31 January 2025, Kristu Jayanti College hosted the One District One Product event under the Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat initiatives, with Shri Pradeep Simha, District Officer of the Minority Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, as chief guest. The university opened its campus as a marketplace through the Campus Farmers Market (Farmers to Students). Twelve farmers from various districts displayed and sold fresh produce, organic goods and traditional food products directly to students, staff and visitors. This gave local producers free access to university facilities and a ready customer base, and removed middlemen so that farmers earned a fairer income. Over 5,000 people benefitted from access to healthy, chemical-free produce and direct interaction with farmers. The event also taught students about the ODOP scheme and how local agriculture, handicrafts and textiles contribute to the economy. It promoted farmer dignity, consumer trust and sustainable local enterprise, and was widely covered by the media.

contentBlocks.title: 3. Launch of the 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme (VADP), Viksit Bharat @2047 (UBA, 23 January 2025)
paragraphs: The Unnat Bharat Abhiyan unit launched the 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme on 23 January 2025 at the Silver Jubilee Auditorium. The university formally committed itself to the long-term development of 25 villages. The thrust areas are holistic wellness, skill development, capacity building, women empowerment, rural entrepreneurship and sustainable development. The programme aims to reduce the socio-economic divide by focusing on marginalised communities and ensuring that economic opportunities reach rural and underdeveloped areas. It plans to create employment through local entrepreneurship, skill-building programmes and infrastructure and development projects. As a body, the university commits its faculty, students and facilities to mentor villagers and run training workshops. The launch brought together the Principal, officials of the Karnataka Slum Development Board and the university community, and was reported in the Malayalam Manorama Bengaluru edition. It forms the framework within which further rural enterprise support activities are carried out.

contentBlocks.title: 4. Cyber Security Awareness Programme, Parehosahalli (UBA, 23 September 2025)
paragraphs: The Unnat Bharat Abhiyan unit, under Jayantian Extension Services, conducted a Cyber Security Awareness Programme at Parehosahalli village, Kolar district, with 25 B.Com Professional Accounting volunteers under Dr. S. Jayashree. Students used visual aids and interactive workshops to demonstrate how phishing and financial scams work. They simplified strong password creation, two-factor authentication and safe online banking into the local language. Participants also received hands-on training in securing their mobile devices and social media accounts. Before the session, residents had low digital literacy, commonly used easily guessable passwords and found it hard to spot phishing attempts. Afterwards they could recognise and describe scam techniques, and many began enabling security features on their devices. Safe digital payments and online banking are essential for small traders, farmers and self-employed residents who run or want to start businesses. The programme protects their finances and builds trust in the digital economy. The Parehosahalli Village Panchayat issued a letter of appreciation.

contentBlocks.title: 5. Vikasa Rural Exposure Camp, Esthuru (UBA, 23 February 2025)
paragraphs: The Vikasa Rural Exposure Camp at Esthuru village began at 5 AM with yoga, followed by a Shramadan in which students cleaned three to four streets, which residents appreciated. Students assisted in the medical camps, where Muthoot conducted blood check-ups and Shankar Eye Hospital provided eye check-ups for villagers. The day also featured the One District One Product scheme and the Campus Farmers Market. Students learned how local agriculture, handicrafts and textiles contribute to the economy and why promoting regional products matters. They interacted directly with local farmers and saw the challenges and opportunities facing local producers first-hand. This motivated them to think creatively about solutions and possible business models for rural producers. The camp combines university volunteers and partner organisations bringing services to the village with a mentoring exchange between students and farmers. It supports sustainable local livelihoods by linking classroom knowledge with real rural enterprise.

contentBlocks.title: 6. Digital Literacy Programme: Paint and MS Word (NSS)
paragraphs: The NSS unit, under Jayantian Extension Services, conducted a hands-on digital literacy workshop for 50 students of K Narayanapura Government School, a neighbouring community with limited access to technology. 16 NSS volunteers trained participants in Paint and MS Word, typing, file management and responsible internet use. The university's expertise and volunteers were offered freely to learners who often have no computer access at home. Sessions were interactive and simplified, so children with little or no prior exposure could build confidence step by step. These are the basic digital skills needed to prepare documents, communicate and use online services, which are the foundation of any future small business or self-employment. By bridging the digital divide for underprivileged learners, the programme equips the community with transferable skills that support economic participation and sustainable livelihoods.

contentBlocks.title: 7. Computer Literacy Programme (NSS)
paragraphs: Under Jayantian Extension Services, NSS volunteers taught students of K Narayanapura Government School the parts of a computer and how to use them. The training covered typing, file management and responsible internet usage through interactive, easy-to-follow methods suited to students with minimal prior exposure. The programme made university knowledge available to a community that would otherwise find such training hard to reach. It reflects the university's commitment to inclusive education and community capacity building. Digital competence is now essential for running any business, whether for record-keeping, communication, marketing or accessing government schemes. Building it early in the local community prepares young people for future employment and entrepreneurship. It also strengthens the long-term link between the university and its neighbourhood.

contentBlocks.title: 8. Teaching Activity: Academic Support, Life Skills and Career Guidance (NSS)
paragraphs: NSS volunteers conducted a structured teaching programme for 45 students of classes 8 and 10, with 12 volunteers contributing. Alongside Hindi instruction, the programme included life skills sessions and career guidance. Volunteers used interactive teaching, problem-solving exercises and motivational sessions to build confidence, and gave special emphasis to exam preparation for class 10 students. It also included career counselling and social awareness discussions, and ended with an evaluation session, feedback collection and distribution of study materials. This works as a mentorship model, with university students helping young people see their options and plan their futures. Career counselling and life skills such as communication, discipline and teamwork are the early building blocks of employability and entrepreneurial thinking. The programme helps first-generation learners stay in education and move towards economically independent lives.

contentBlocks.title: 9. Skill Enhancement Activity: Hindi Language and Communication (NSS)
paragraphs: Supervised by Mr. Mohammed Nayaz Pasha of the Department of Hindi, four NSS volunteers conducted a skill enhancement activity at Sri Siddhartha Sanivasa Government School, Narayanapura, for students of classes 9 and 10. The workshop focused on vocabulary, reading and comprehension, and used group discussions to improve speaking and listening skills. Students regarded the topic as a need of the hour for Hindi language learning, and showed noticeably greater confidence in using the language afterwards. Communication ability is a core skill for any entrepreneur, and it also opens employment opportunities for young people from modest backgrounds. The activity is an example of university faculty and student volunteers offering structured training workshops to local students. Over time, such skill-building improves employability and the ability to engage with customers, markets and institutions.

contentBlocks.title: 10. NSS Special Annual Camp 2025–26: Health, Digital Safety and ABHA Support (Sonnenahalli and Seeresandra, 11–17 October 2025)
paragraphs: During the seven-day special camp, NSS volunteers ran practical awareness and service programmes in Sonnenahalli and Seeresandra villages. Free eye check-ups, BP and sugar screening and blood donation awareness reached about 115 villagers, and 67 received free spectacles. On Day 4 a Cyber Crime Awareness Session taught villagers safe internet practices and how to recognise fraud calls and messages. Volunteers also went door to door to promote ABHA health cards, and on Day 5 they helped villagers create 34 ABHA cards. Cleanliness drives, tree plantation and an alumni talk were part of the camp. The digital safety and ABHA sessions give villagers the awareness needed to use digital services, payments and government schemes securely, which small local businesses and self-employed residents depend on. Health screening and spectacles also protect people's ability to work. Collaborations with Rotary clubs and the local Grama Panchayats brought university resources to the community.

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), through Jayantian Extension Services and its student units (CSA, NSS, KCDC and UBA), works with government bodies to put national, state and local anti-poverty policy into practice in the communities around it. The university works with local self-government bodies such as Gram Panchayats and the BBMP, takes part in flagship schemes such as Unnat Bharat Abhiyan, Ayushman Bharat (ABHA), Swachh Bharat, One District One Product and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, and hosts government officials at its events. Through these partnerships the university takes policy on rural development, livelihoods, health access, sanitation and girls' education to poor and rural households. It also builds long-term relationships with village administrations, which supports its continued participation in local and national development programmes.

contentBlocks.title: Programmes
1. Launch of the 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme (VADP), Viksit Bharat @2047 (UBA, 23/01/2025)
paragraphs: Chief guest was Dr. Ashok D. R., KAS, Commissioner, Karnataka Slum Development Board. The university formally committed itself to the long-term development of 25 adopted villages focusing on holistic wellness, skill development, women empowerment and rural entrepreneurship.

contentBlocks.title: 2. One District One Product (ODOP) and Campus Farmers Market (UBA, 31/01/2025)
paragraphs: The chief guest was Shri Pradeep Simha, District Officer, Minority Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka. Twelve farmers took part, and over 5,000 people benefitted from direct marketing access on campus without middlemen.

contentBlocks.title: 3. ABHA Card Awareness and Registration Drives (CSA and NSS, 2025)
paragraphs: Under the national Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, 85 families at Shivagange (January) and 44 families (1 April) were reached, and 34 ABHA cards were created at the NSS camp (15 October).

contentBlocks.title: 4. Blackspot Cleaning Drive with BBMP (JES and KCDC, 07/10/2024)
paragraphs: 50 volunteers collected over 200 kg of litter and plastic and cleaned more than 1,000 sq. ft. in collaboration with the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP).

contentBlocks.title: 5. NSS Special Annual Camp with Gram Panchayats of Sonnenahalli and Kanasawadi (11/10/2025 – 17/10/2025)
paragraphs: About 115 villagers were screened and 67 received free spectacles, with ABHA and cyber awareness sessions organized in coordination with local Panchayat administration.

contentBlocks.title: 6. Gram Swachh Abhiyan, Parehosahalli (UBA, 23/09/2025)
paragraphs: Held with Panchayat members and Swachh Bharat Mission coordinators, with 25 volunteers, and the Panchayat issued a letter of appreciation.

contentBlocks.title: 7. Street Play on Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (KCDC with the Theatre Club)
paragraphs: Promoted the national campaign for girls' education and protection through community theatrical performances.

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) follows Sustainable Development Goal 1 (No Poverty) through Jayantian Extension Services (JES), its institutional outreach and societal engagement division, and the centres and wings that work alongside it. JES was started to promote social concern and good citizenship, and its objectives are to assess community needs, build institution-neighbourhood networks and promote the holistic development of nearby villages. Its wings, Centre for Social Activities, National Service Scheme , Karnataka Civil Defence Corps (KCDC) ,Unnat Bharat Abhiyan(UBA) and Youth Red Cross take students and faculty into villages and communities. Allied bodies add livelihood and entrepreneurship support, gender equality, inclusion of marginalised students and environmental responsibility. Together they aim to address poverty-related needs in education, health, livelihood, rights and access to government schemes.

contentBlocks.title: Table of Events
Jayantian Extension Services — Centre for Social Activities (CSA)
rows: Life Skill Programme

Conducted during the CSA rural exposure camp at Shivagange, Adime, Kolar. Student volunteers ran a life skill programme for rural school students covering communication, problem-solving, teamwork and time management. Hands-on workshops built confidence, and guidance on emotional intelligence and stress management was given. The programme aimed to narrow the skill gap between rural and urban students.
70 volunteers; 51 students of Govt. Primary School, Shivagange benefitted.
Career Guidance Programme

A career guidance session at the Shivagange camp helped students make informed decisions about their future. It covered career options, skills required and the role of personal interests. Industry experts and alumni shared experiences, and participants were guided on resumes, interviews and networking, with workshops on time management and goal setting.
70 volunteers; 65 participants gained awareness of career options and readiness for the professional world.
Shramadhaan

A Shramadhaan drive was held to clean and beautify the premises at the Shivagange camp. Volunteers swept and cleaned the toilet areas and surroundings and removed excess grass from the gardens. The drive instilled pride and teamwork and promoted collective ownership and civic responsibility.
70 volunteers; improved access to hygienic sanitation facilities for disadvantaged households.
Interaction with SHG Women

Students held an interactive session with rural women on the benefits and working of Self-Help Groups. It explained how SHGs provide financial support, skill development and a platform for collective decision-making, covered forming and managing a group and the value of savings and microfinance, and shared success stories.
70 volunteers; 65 women of Shivagange village benefitted.
ABHA Registration Drive

Students set up registration booths and helped villagers fill in forms for ABHA health cards. They explained how the card improves access to healthcare, reaching first-time users and people without digital access, and supported each person until registration was completed.
70 volunteers; 85 families of Shivagange village benefitted.
Community Education Programme – Lessons from Life

Alumni guests conducted the activity “Lessons from Life”, sharing personal and professional experiences with students at the Shivagange camp. A fun game session broke the ice and a Q&A gave students the chance to seek advice. The interaction was informal, interactive and enriching.
51 students of Govt. Primary School, Shivagange benefitted.
Sports for School Children

Volunteers organised a sports day for school children at the camp with games such as soccer, basketball and athletics. The activities kept children active and healthy, built teamwork and confidence, and promoted a lifelong love for sports.
21 children participated.
Rural Social Networking

Students interacted with villagers to share modern farming techniques – precision farming, organic fertilisers, water conservation and eco-friendly pest management. They also listened to farmers’ concerns such as limited access to technology, finance and erratic weather, building understanding between the academic and farming communities.
Villagers gained awareness of sustainable farming practices; students gained first-hand insight into rural farming realities.
Awareness Campaign on Government Schemes (ABHA Card)

Students explained the significance of the ABHA card and how it improves access to healthcare under government schemes. They gave step-by-step registration guidance, helped villagers register on-site and addressed concerns about the process so that health services become more accessible and secure.
44 families benefitted; villagers gained knowledge of health coverage and registered for ABHA cards.
Bhavishyajyothi 2025 – Fundraising Campaign

A CSA fundraising campaign for educating underprivileged children and developing rural sanitation, inaugurated by Fr. Jais V. Thomas. Funds were raised through food, henna, games and article stalls (including an unattended “Integrity Stall”), class-to-class donations, and “If Not You, Then Who” stickers carrying a QR code to CSA’s Instagram page.
Funds raised support education and sanitation initiatives for underprivileged children; fostered trust and social responsibility.
Computer Literacy Programme

Held in the M1 Lab for children of migrant workers who have limited access to technology. Children were introduced to computer hardware, software and simple applications through interactive, hands-on activities that built curiosity and confidence in using digital tools.
Children learned basic computer parts and simple applications, gained confidence and were motivated to continue digital learning.
Sarthakam – Clothes Collection Drive

A campus clothes collection drive, “Sarthakam: Not Just Shared – Made Meaningful”. Faculty were approached and awareness sessions held on 4 and 8 September. Collection boxes and placards were placed across the campus from 3 September, monitored regularly, and the clothes were sorted and stored in the CSA room.
Encouraging response from students and faculty; clothes collected and sorted for donation.
Pratyasha’s – Annadasooha

Student volunteers prepared and packed wholesome meals and served them at the slum area near the college. They shared food with residents of all age groups – children, adults and the elderly – and interacted warmly with them, extending kindness through the simple act of sharing food.
Meals shared with slum residents; volunteers built compassion and community connect.
Life Skill Activities – Rural Exposure Camp (Samayak Samruddhi)

Life skill sessions for children of Ittasandra, Hoskote, using interactive activities, storytelling and games to teach communication, teamwork, personal hygiene and problem-solving. The sessions aimed to build self-confidence, active participation and healthy habits.
Rural Children showed improved communication, teamwork, hygiene awareness, problem-solving and confidence.
Cancer Prevention and Screening Camp

Organised at Esthuru Village, Hoskote, to promote early detection of breast, cervical and oral cancers among villagers, children and volunteers. A medical team from the Indian Cancer Society led by Dr. Pavithra and Dr. Pavan Kumar conducted screening and counselled participants on symptoms, risk factors, follow-up care and lifestyle.
Villagers gained awareness of cancer prevention and warning signs; several were screened; fear of screening reduced.
Science Model Explanation for School Kids of Ittasandra

Volunteers explained human-body science models – heart, lungs, digestive system, head, arms and legs – to school children of Ittasandra in simple language, using questions and demonstrations. The activity linked classroom learning with real-world demonstration in a rural school.
Children understood basic biological concepts and showed greater curiosity and interest in science.
National Eye Checkup Camp

An eye checkup camp at Esthuru Village, Hoskote, inaugurated by Fr. Jais V. Thomas and Fr. Som Zacharias and coordinated with Rotary Bengaluru Alumni. Eye examinations were conducted by Modi High Hospital staff, with vision testing and screening for villagers and volunteers.
Accessible eye-care services provided to villagers; awareness raised on eye health and regular vision screening.

contentBlocks.title: National Service Scheme (NSS)
rows: Skill Enhancement Activity

Four NSS volunteers, supervised by Mr. Mohammed Nayaz Pasha (Dept. of Hindi), conducted a Hindi language activity at Sri Siddhartha Sanivasa Government School, Narayanapura for students of classes 9 and 10. It focused on vocabulary, reading and comprehension, with group discussions to improve speaking and listening skills.
Students of classes 9 and 10th government school, showed enhanced confidence in Hindi; 4 volunteers.
Computer Literacy Programme

NSS volunteers, guided by Dr. Margaret Mary T, taught students of K Narayanapura Government School the basic parts of a computer and their use. Hands-on, easy-to-follow sessions covered typing, file management and responsible internet usage for students with little or no prior exposure.
Government students gained basic digital skills and confidence, helping bridge the digital divide.
Shiksha Setu – Snack Distribution

Under Dr. Vinoth B, NSS volunteers organised a snack distribution drive for government school children at K Narayanapura, Bengaluru. Snacks such as samosas, chocolates, pencils and energy bars were given to support the well-being and attentiveness of underprivileged children.
Underprivileged children supported; volunteers learned the value of empathy and service.
Digital Literacy Programme (Paint and MS Word)

NSS volunteers, guided by Dr. Margaret Mary T, taught K Narayanapura Government School students basic computer skills including Paint and MS Word, typing, file management and responsible internet use. Complex topics were simplified for children new to technology.
50 Government school students benefitted; 16 NSS volunteers.
Teaching Activity

Academic support for students of classes 8 and 10, focusing on Hindi along with life skills and career guidance. Volunteers used interactive teaching, problem-solving exercises and motivational sessions, with exam-preparation techniques for class 10, ending with evaluation, feedback and distribution of study materials.
45 students benefitted; 12 volunteers.
Little Hands, Big Creations

An outreach programme for 5th-grade students at a government school led by Ms Shreya Thomas. Fun games improved teamwork, problem-solving and coordination, while crafts and drawing activities let children express ideas visually and nurtured confidence and imagination.
75 government school students benefitted; 27 volunteers.
Share the Knowledge, Share the Health

An awareness session for 7th-grade students of a government school on handwashing and personal hygiene, delivered in English and Kannada under Ms Shreya Thomas. Volunteers demonstrated step-by-step handwashing and held interactive discussions on how cleanliness prevents illness.
100 government school students benefitted; 27 volunteers; hygiene, nutrition and study habits covered.
Nurturing the Young Minds

Five NSS volunteers led by group heads Shalini I and John Cherian, under Mr. Madhusudhanan, conducted a one-hour outreach at K. Narayanapura Government School. They taught Kannada, English, Mathematics and games, and used moral stories and discussions to learn students’ interests and learning levels.
30 government school students benefitted; 5 volunteers.
Visit to Neha Jyothi Ashram

Volunteers from two NSS teams collected donations and visited Neha Jyothi Ashram with snacks. They played games such as passing the ball and musical chairs, organised singing and dancing to showcase talents, gave prizes to winners and served snacks to the children.
15 Ashram children benefitted; ₹2,000 donations collected; 5 volunteers.
Visit to refuge Foundation

Twelve NSS volunteers under Mr. Mayank David visited the Refuge Foundation, played games with the children and distributed healthier snacks and stationery kits. The visit encouraged reflection on social responsibility and the impact of small acts of kindness.
20 children benefitted; ₹2,000 spent on essentials; 12 volunteers.
Activity on Keeping Clean and Healthy

Eight NSS volunteers led by Akash B R and Monisha RJ, under Dr. Krishna D Lamani, held a hygiene awareness programme at Sri Siddhartha Sanivasa High School, Narayanapura. Topics included handwashing, sanitation, waste management and personal hygiene, supported by posters and a documentary on public health.
150 high school students benefitted; 8 volunteers.
Shramadhan

Twelve NSS volunteers led by Hari Narayanan T B and Deepika, under Dr. Jeeva M, cleaned public spaces and removed waste outside the campus. They also spread awareness on hygiene, sustainable practices and responsible waste management among local residents.
800 local residents benefitted; 12 volunteers.
A Little Help Goes a Long Way – Stationery Distribution

In collaboration with Radiant Life Charitable Trust, Geddalahalli, an NGO supporting over 250 children, NSS volunteers led by Ms Shreya Thomas distributed stationery kits so that children have the basic supplies needed for learning, and built a warm bond with the community.
Stationery worth ₹4,000 donated by teachers and students; 400 beneficiaries recorded; 4 volunteers.
Cleaning Surroundings

Thirty-seven NSS volunteers, working in groups with trash bags and gloves provided by faculty, cleaned areas near Kristu Jayanti College, Kothanur. The drive built leadership, teamwork and civic responsibility and encouraged residents to keep surroundings clean.
About 600 local residents benefitted; 37 volunteers.
Donate and Delight

Thirty-nine NSS volunteers led by Akash B R and Monisha RJ, under Dr. Krishna D Lamani, held a programme on the importance of education and learning tools, including a short educational video. Volunteers organised, sorted and distributed donated items to children.
Essential items worth ₹4,500 collected; 50 children benefitted; 39 volunteers.
Feed the Hunger

NSS volunteers collected and distributed meals to needy individuals and families at K. Narayanapura, together with an awareness campaign on hunger, malnutrition and food waste. Students developed empathy and communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills.
20 needy families benefitted; ₹5,000 raised through donations; 8 volunteers.
Offering to the Needy

Forty-six NSS volunteers led by group heads Shalini I and John Cherian, under Mr. Madhusudhanan, visited K. Narayanapura Government School. A one-hour interactive session of games and activities was held and essential stationery was donated to children from marginalised families.
20 children benefitted; ₹1,200 spent on stationery; 46 volunteers.
Pencils of Hope

NSS volunteers under Dr. Jeeva M collected and donated stationery to under-resourced students, alongside a “Learn Kannada Talk Kannada” activity. The drive supports learning continuity, helps reduce dropout rates and promotes the value of education.
30 children benefitted; ₹2,000 raised; 4 volunteers actively participated.
Cleanliness Drive – Kothanur Government School

NSS volunteers cleared litter, plastic waste and garbage in and around Kothanur Government School in support of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan. The drive concluded with a collective pledge to continue working for a cleaner, greener future.
Visibly cleaner school surroundings; strengthened civic responsibility among volunteers.
NSS Special Annual Camp 2025–26 – Day 1 (Inauguration and Orientation)

Volunteers reached Seeresandra, Sonnenahalli Gram Panchayat, for the inauguration by Gram Panchayat member Mr. Krishnappa Gowda. Programme Officers Dr. Muhammad Nayaz Pasha, Dr. Margaret Mary T and Dr. Vidyavathi R conducted the orientation, and volunteers were divided into five groups – Vaayu, Jala, Agni, Bhumi and Akasha.
Team spirit built; rapport established with village representatives and an encouraging, disciplined atmosphere set for the camp.
NSS Special Annual Camp 2025–26 – Day 2 (Shramadan and Health Camps)

Shramadan at the Primary Health Centre, Govt. Primary School and Byatha Grama Panchayat, followed by free eye check-ups, a blood donation awareness programme and BP and sugar check-ups in collaboration with Rotary Bangalore Assare and Rotary Bangalore Downtowners.
About 115 villagers received free health check-ups and 67 received free spectacles; improved hygiene at PHC, panchayat and school.
NSS Special Annual Camp 2025–26 – Day 3 (Cleanliness and Community Outreach)

The day began at 5 a.m. with prayer, exercise and flag hoisting, followed by cleaning of Govt. Primary School Byatha, Ambedkar Bhavan and temple surroundings. Volunteers visited nearby villages to invite residents to the Cyber Awareness Programme; the evening had cultural events and a reflection session.
Villagers informed of the cyber awareness programme; cleaner public spaces; stronger trust between NSS and the community.
NSS Special Annual Camp 2025–26 – Day 4 (Cyber Crime and ABHA Awareness)

Cleaning inside and around the Seeresandra temple, food distribution to villagers and flag hoisting. A Cyber Crime Awareness Session covered safe internet practices and fraud calls/messages, and groups went door to door to spread awareness about the ABHA card and invite villagers to the creation camp.
Villagers understood digital safety and the value of ABHA cards; many keen to attend the card creation camp.
NSS Special Annual Camp 2025–26 – Day 5 (ABHA Card Creation and Tree Plantation)

Cleanliness drive at the Veterinary Hospital, bus stop and temples of Seeresandra, followed by flag hoisting, an alumni talk and tree plantation on school premises. NSS volunteers helped villagers create ABHA cards, and the day ended with cultural skits; leftover food was donated to villagers.
34 ABHA cards created for villagers; cleaner public areas; trees planted; stronger community bond.
NSS Donation Drive – Essentials and Clothing for the Needy

Eleven B.Com NSS volunteers under Ms. Simi Anto collected and distributed clothes and daily necessities to families at the Narayanapura slum near the university, promoting empathy, reuse, sharing and sustainable practices.
25 needy beneficiaries received essentials and clothing; volunteers built empathy and teamwork.
Shield Up: Safety and Protection for Young Minds

Nineteen volunteers under Mr. Prakash K P visited Infant Jesus Children’s Home, Agram. Four teams delivered presentations, poster-based explanations, interactive Q&A and inspirational stories on road safety, online safety, stranger danger and hygiene, and donated notebooks and pens.
70 children benefitted; improved confidence and recall of safety tips.
Awareness Session on Values, Life Skills and Social Awareness

Fifteen BCA and BA volunteers under Ms A S Manjari taught classes 1–5 of Government Model Higher Primary School, Kothanur, through stories, games and demonstrations on decision-making, gender equality, environmental awareness and respect. A first-aid kit was donated to the school.
115 Government school children benefitted; school–university connection strengthened.
Empowering Women through Hygiene and Education

Six volunteers under Mrs. Resmi T J held a menstrual hygiene awareness session at The Refuge Foundation, with group discussion to break myths and taboos. They donated 25 packs of sanitary pads, soaps, mosquito repellent cards, hand wash and washing powder.
14 refugee beneficiaries gained hygiene awareness and essential products.
Healthcare Awareness Programme

Volunteers under Dr. Arunkumar B visited Government School, Northwoods Layout, Vaddarapalya, to teach handwashing, bathing, dental care, balanced diets, prevention of malaria, dengue and anaemia, and mental well-being, with a short yoga session for the children.
35 Government School children benefitted; adoption of healthier daily routines.
Empowering Education

NSS volunteers under Dr. K. Jagannathan distributed essential learning materials to students of Government Model Higher Primary School, Kothanur, and held interactive sessions on education, personal hygiene and goal setting, with storytelling and games.
40 children benefitted; strengthened bond between NSS and the school.
First Aid Awareness

Twenty-two first-year B.Sc. Forensic Science volunteers led by Angel Maria and Manikantan, under Mr. Raiborde Mayank David, taught children of Government Upper Primary School, K Narayanapura, basic first aid for cuts, burns, nosebleeds and fainting, encouraging calm and responsible action.
40 children benefitted; confidence to handle minor emergencies.
Assertiveness Training

Six NSS volunteers and two group heads, guided by Ms. Hrithikaa A (Dept. of Psychology), conducted interactive sessions for 32 grade-5 students of Government Model Primary School, Kothanur, on assertiveness and decision-making, including how to interact with elders and how to say no.
32 students gained confidence in expressing opinions respectfully and setting boundaries.
Health and Nutrition Awareness Programme

Volunteers under Dr. Merrin R S visited a government school to explain the importance of fruits, vegetables and whole grains, avoiding junk food, drinking enough water, regular exercise and personal hygiene. Pencils and erasers were distributed as tokens of encouragement.
Students understood healthy food choices and hygiene and participated actively.
A Kit of Hope – Distribution of Study Materials

Under Ms. Anna Pops (Dept. of Physical Sciences), NSS volunteers distributed study kits of notebooks, pencils, pens, colours, scales and erasers to underprivileged children at K. Narayanapura, interacting warmly to encourage regular schooling and creativity.
Children received essential study materials; improved motivation, confidence and interest in education.

contentBlocks.title: Karnataka Civil Defence Corps (KCDC)
rows: Manovikas – Mental Health Awareness for Security and Housekeeping Staff

KCDC organised the “Manovikas” awareness programme in the H1 Auditorium for security personnel and housekeeping staff, led by consultant psychologist Ms. Ambika Avadam of Swasthmind & Manonetra. It covered stress management, coping mechanisms and building a supportive work environment.
Frontline staff gained knowledge on mental health, stress management and emotional resilience.
Yuva Avishkar – Lab on Wheels Launch

Jayantian Extension Services inaugurated “Yuva Avishkar – Lab on Wheels” at the A3 Auditorium, Admin Block, with Mr. K.N. Prabhakaran (Head CSR, L&T Technologies) and Fr. Jais V. Thomas. The initiative takes interactive STEM models to school children who lack access to such resources.
218 participants; 15 STEM working models; 70% of underprivileged children showed increased STEM interest.
Dengue Awareness Activity

KCDC held a dengue awareness activity at Nagenahalli and K. Narayanapura with awareness sessions, bilingual pamphlets, a community clean-up to remove stagnant water, demonstrations on repellents and nets, and quizzes for children.
150+ community members reached; 25 volunteers; 85% of residents willing to adopt prevention practices.
Blackspot Cleaning

Jayantian Extension Services with BBMP organised a blackspot cleaning drive near the college. Volunteers with gloves and masks collected and segregated dry waste, especially plastics, into separate bins for recycling, and ended with a reflection on waste segregation.
50 volunteers; 1,000+ sq. ft. cleaned; 200+ kg of litter and plastic collected.
Joy of Giving – Blessed Clare Special School

On Children’s Day, KCDC visited Blessed Clare Special School, donating notebooks, pen sets, pencils, erasers, colouring supplies, biscuits and cookies. Volunteers celebrated with singing and dancing, creating a joyful atmosphere with the children.
50 children benefitted; 200+ stationery items distributed.
Computer Literacy – Kothanur Government School

KCDC volunteers taught students of Kothanur Government School basic computer operations, internet usage and MS Office, including typing documents, browsing safely and using digital tools for education.
100+ students trained; 90% reported improved digital confidence; 85% showed proficiency.
Literacy and Sports Programme – Annihalli

At Annihalli Primary School (28 Feb, 2:30–4:30 PM), students of grades 1–7 played relay games with prizes. On 1 March volunteers conducted an interactive literacy session at a local high school using engaging, creative methods.
Students engaged in joyful learning; volunteers gained leadership and communication experience.
Yuva Avishkar Science Exhibition – Annihalli

KCDC volunteers presented interactive physics, biology and chemistry models at Government High School, Annihalli, Kolar. They explained how each model works and encouraged students to ask questions and experiment, presenting complex scientific concepts in a hands-on manner.
Rural students experienced hands-on STEM learning beyond textbooks. 57 beneficiaries; sparked curiosity in students; volunteers built communication and teamwork skills.
Visit to Health Department, Kolar District

KCDC volunteers visited the health department in Kolar district, interacting with medical staff and observing preventive and curative programmes, with emphasis on maternal health, child vaccination and government healthcare schemes.
Volunteers gained first-hand exposure to rural healthcare and can share health awareness with villagers.
Computer Literacy Programme
Revision and interactive sessions on computer basics, characteristics, generations and classification, with practical training in MS Word and MS Excel, delivered by KCDC volunteers to students.
Students strengthened fundamental computer knowledge and practical skills.

contentBlocks.title: Under Youth Red Cross (YRC)
rows: Experiential Learning – Visit to Migrant Labourers’ Settlement

Following an expert talk, teams visited the migrant labourers’ settlement at K Narayanapura to collect data on demographics, income, education, health, sanitation, housing and water supply through one-on-one interviews and observation of living conditions.
Socio-economic data documented; volunteers understood community conditions first-hand.
Together We Feed

YRC volunteers visited Ananda Sagara, an organisation supporting underprivileged children, engaged the children in educational and fun activities and served nutritious meals, aiming to raise Rs. 3,500 and foster empathy and social responsibility.
Food worth ₹4,000 distributed; children developed teamwork and communication skills.
Platter of Hope – Charity Stalls

YRC volunteers ran charity stalls offering homemade food, juices, games and handmade jewellery to raise funds for underprivileged communities. The event drew enthusiastic participation from students and faculty and gave volunteers hands-on experience in event management.
89 volunteers participated; funds raised for underprivileged communities.
Kits of Care – Migrant Settlement, Kothanur

With 22 volunteers from I MA English Literature and the SDG Club, stationery kits with notebooks, pencils, erasers, sharpeners, rulers and crayons were assembled from donations and distributed to children of the Kothanur migrant settlement.
Stationery given to nearly 35 migrant children; boosted enthusiasm for learning.

contentBlocks.title: Under Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA)
rows: Launch of 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme (VADP)

The 25 Village Adoption and Development Programme (Viksit Bharat @2047) was launched at the Silver Jubilee Auditorium. It targets holistic wellness, skill development, capacity building, women empowerment, rural entrepreneurship and sustainable development of adopted villages.
25 villages adopted; reported in Malayalam Manorama (Bengaluru edition).
One District One Product (ODOP) – Campus Farmers Market

The college hosted the ODOP event to promote local products and rural economic development, with Shri. Pradeep Simha as chief guest. The Campus Farmers Market let 12 farmers sell fresh, organic and traditional products directly to the public.
12 farmers; over 5,000 people benefitted from chemical-free produce; farmers’ income supported without middlemen.
Vikasa – Rural Exposure Camp, Esthuru

The day began with yoga and a Shramadan covering 3–4 streets of Esthuru. Students assisted at medical camps – Muthoot conducted blood checkups and Shankar Eye Hospital eye checkups – and learned about ODOP and local produce.
Villagers benefitted from free blood and eye check-ups; streets cleaned.
Gram Swachh Abhiyan
A village cleanliness drive at Parehosahalli, Kolar. Litter was cleared from streets and drainage paths, and villagers were educated on sanitation and waste segregation.
Visible reduction of litter; residents keen to set up community dustbins; appreciation letter from the Panchayat.
Cyber Security Awareness Programme

At Parehosahalli, volunteers used visual aids and workshops to show how phishing and financial scams work, taught strong passwords, two-factor authentication and safe online banking in the local language, and trained villagers to secure phones and social media accounts.
Villagers can recognise scams and began adopting safer digital practices; 25 volunteers.

title: Policy addressing poverty
subtitle: Institutional Policies, Wings and Strategic Frameworks Addressing Poverty

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University) follows Sustainable Development Goal 1 (No Poverty) through Jayantian Extension Services (JES), its institutional outreach and societal engagement division, and the centres and wings that work alongside it. JES was started to promote social concern and good citizenship, and its objectives are to assess community needs, build institution-neighbourhood networks and promote the holistic development of nearby villages. Its wings, Centre for Social Activities, National Service Scheme , Karnataka Civil Defence Corps (KCDC) ,Unnat Bharat Abhiyan(UBA) and Youth Red Cross take students and faculty into villages and communities. Allied bodies add livelihood and entrepreneurship support, gender equality, inclusion of marginalised students and environmental responsibility. Together they aim to address poverty-related needs in education, health, livelihood, rights and access to government schemes.

contentBlocks.title: 1. Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA)
paragraphs: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan applies the university's knowledge to rural development in line with the Government of India's UBA programme. In 2025 the unit adopted 25 villages under the Ittasandra, Hettakki, Annihalli and Marjenahalli panchayats in Hosakote Taluk (Bengaluru Rural) and Kolar Taluk (Kolar). It draws on 18 departments, 5 Jayantian Extension Services units and several centres. Its policy requires liaison with village panchayats, government offices and the UBA Regional Coordinating Institute, plus village situation analysis and need assessment. UBA has many outreach activities which include financial literacy, micro-savings, digital literacy, women's employability, awareness of government schemes, farmer training on crop yields, an organic farm, health and nutrition camps, and sanitation drives. Executed 2024-25 activities include a special camp, social outreach and Shramadhan.
Institutional Reference Portal: https://kristujayanti.edu.in/uba

contentBlocks.title: 2. National Service Scheme (NSS)
paragraphs: The NSS unit engages undergraduate students in voluntary community service, Its policy aims to help students understand community needs, solve local problems, mobilise community participation and build civic responsibility. It works for the integrated development of adopted villages and slums through regular and special camps. Its fields of work include literacy, health and family welfare, disaster management and the environment. At least one hundred students enrol each year. Past campaigns covered AIDS awareness, legal awareness, the rights and status of women, child welfare, water conservation, pest control and tree plantation. The mission is to help higher education institutions work with rural India on development challenges and sustainable growth.
Institutional Reference Portal: https://kristujayanti.edu.in/jes/nss

contentBlocks.title: 3. Entrepreneurship and Innovation Centre (EIC)
paragraphs: The Entrepreneurship and Innovation Centre builds livelihood and income opportunities by supporting start-ups, innovation and social entrepreneurship among students, faculty and alumni. The Centre offers entrepreneurship development programmes, pre-incubation and incubation support, business plan competitions and mentoring. It also provides co-working and prototype infrastructure and a university seed fund where available. Founders are linked to government schemes such as Startup India, DST and MSME, and to angel investors and grants. Partnerships with incubators, accelerators, MSMEs and government agencies are part of its mandate. An Advisory Committee that includes external experts and alumni entrepreneurs reviews the policy annually. Its stated mission is to contribute to socio-economic development.
Institutional Reference Portal: https://kristujayanti.edu.in/student-services/eic

contentBlocks.title: 4. Centre for Social Activities (CSA)
paragraphs: The Centre for Social Activities (CSA) at Kristu Jayanti University serves as an institutional platform for promoting social responsibility, community engagement and sustainable development. Established in 2009, CSA encourages students to participate in humanitarian service and contribute towards meaningful social transformation. The Centre undertakes various outreach programmes aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), focusing particularly on the welfare of underprivileged and underserved communities. Its initiatives include rural exposure camps, health check-up camps, blood donation drives, computer literacy programmes, awareness campaigns on social issues and educational sponsorships for school children. CSA seeks to improve access to education, healthcare, digital literacy and essential resources. The Centre also collaborates with NGOs to strengthen institutional relationships with local communities. These initiatives provide students with opportunities to translate institutional values into meaningful community service. By addressing social inequalities and improving the quality of life of disadvantaged sections of society, CSA contributes to inclusive and sustainable community development.
Institutional Reference Portal: https://kristujayanti.edu.in/jes/csa/

contentBlocks.title: 5. Youth Red Cross (YRC)
paragraphs: The Youth Red Cross (YRC) wing of Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), a Jayantian Extension Services wing, operates within the Indian Red Cross Society's national structure, which runs from national headquarters through state, district and taluk branches. YRC policy places the wing under a University Nodal Officer and a District YRC Sub-Committee, so its programmes follow a humanitarian framework set beyond the campus. The college Advisory Committee, chaired by the Principal, includes a representative of the district or taluk branch of the Indian Red Cross Society. Each year the Programme Officer submits an annual and activity report to the University Nodal Officer, and the policy commits the wing to collaborate with other humanitarian organisations. At the local level, the February 2025 survey at the K. Narayanapura migrant settlement documented demographics, income, education, health, sanitation, housing and water supply, which is the kind of data local anti-poverty planning needs. The wing's policy also commits it to disaster preparedness training with experts and to community service for marginalised communities.
Institutional Reference Portal: https://kristujayanti.edu.in/jes/yrc/
